title: The Witness of the Marlowe Estate Anew
premise: True-crime podcaster Edmund Vasquez arrives in the fog-bound town of Marlowe's Crossing to cover the centennial exhumation of its beloved founder, Abigail Marlowe, whose 1924 death remains the coldest case on record. When the coffin proves empty, Edmund realizes someone in town has known the truth for a century—and that her own family history is tangled in the cover-up. As she records interviews, she discovers the killer is feeding her clues, testing whether loyalty to the town's 'found family' legacy will outweigh the truth. In the end, Edmund exposes that Abigail faked her own death to escape a murderous husband, and his descendants have been killing ever since to protect the myth—forcing Edmund to choose between the town that embraced her and the story that could destroy it.
about_author: Oscar Iversen is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering unsolved cases across New England before turning to fiction. They live near the coast with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy archive of microfilmed obituaries.

chapters.title: The Centennial Invitation
chapters.summary: Edmund Vasquez, POV. Edmund arrives in Marlowe's Crossing to record the ceremonial exhumation of founder Abigail Marlowe, hoping the publicity will revive her struggling podcast. The town welcomes her with unsettling warmth. Emotional beat: cautious optimism shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: An Empty Box
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Before a crowd of townsfolk and cameras, the coffin is opened—and empty except for a century-old ledger page. The mayor demands discretion; Edmund smells a story. Emotional beat: shock hardening into professional hunger as she pockets the page.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Digging through the historical society's sealed basement with young archivist Theo Brandt, she finds gaps in the 1924 records—pages razored out with surgical care. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into unease at how tidy the omissions are.

chapters.title: Voices of the Old Families
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. She interviews three descendants of the founding families; each recites identical, rehearsed details about Abigail's death. One, Cordelia Ash, slips and mentions a second grave. Emotional beat: mounting suspicion beneath polite hospitality.

chapters.title: What the Microphone Caught
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Reviewing raw audio, Edmund hears a faint third voice on her interview recordings—someone feeding answers off-mic. The voice matches the town historian, Silas Wren. Emotional beat: vindication laced with fear that she's being managed.

chapters.title: A Note in Her Own Hand
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. An anonymous letter arrives quoting Edmund's private doubts back to her, written in Abigail's documented handwriting style. Whoever sent it knows the case file better than any investigator alive. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is also prey.

chapters.title: Theo's Confession
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Theo admits he was paid by Silas to steer Edmund away from certain boxes, but he kept copies of everything. He gives her a photograph of Abigail alive in 1931. Emotional beat: found-family warmth between Edmund and Theo, and shared resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Following Cordelia's slip, they locate an unmarked grave on the old Ash property containing a woman who died decades after Abigail supposedly did—with Abigail's wedding ring. Emotional beat: awe giving way to dread of what the myth protected.

chapters.title: Silas Wren's Sermon
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas reflects on a century of his family guarding the town's story, convinced the lie is a kindness that holds Marlowe's Crossing together. He decides Edmund must be turned or buried. Emotional beat: chilling sincerity—the villain who believes he's a shepherd.

chapters.title: Fire at the Historical Society
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The archive burns overnight; Theo is hospitalized escaping with one box. Among the salvaged papers: Abigail's diary naming her husband's violence and her plan to vanish. Emotional beat: grief and fury, loyalty to Theo cementing Edmund's purpose.

chapters.title: The Podcast That Wasn't Mine
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. A rival feed posts episodes using Edmund's stolen research, twisting the narrative to frame a dead drifter for murder. Someone inside her circle leaked files. Emotional beat: betrayal and isolation—her invisibility gone, her tools weaponized.

chapters.title: Cordelia Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Cordelia, POV. Cordelia reveals the founding families' pact: protect the myth, share the profits, bury dissenters. Her brother vanished in 1987 asking too many questions. Emotional beat: a defector's trembling courage, offering Edmund the map of complicity.

chapters.title: Nineteen Twenty-Four, Retold
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Reconstructing from the diary: Abigail staged her death with the help of household staff who became the founding families—loyalty bought with silence. Emotional beat: tragic understanding; the town's warmth was built on a corpse that never existed.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Sprung Backward
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Edmund stages a fake discovery to flush the killer, but Silas anticipated it—he's read her notes, her drafts, even her therapy-adjacent journaling left on her laptop. Emotional beat: humbling terror; she has been out-planned at every turn.

chapters.title: Held in the Founder's House
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Silas detains Edmund in the Marlowe homestead, arguing the town needs its legend more than its truth, and offers her partnership: co-author the myth. Emotional beat: temptation—belonging offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: Theo's Long Walk
chapters.summary: Theo, POV. Discharged early and terrified, Theo smuggles Edmund's hidden backup drive to Cordelia and rallies the younger generation of townsfolk who never took the oath. Emotional beat: found family becoming a resistance.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Page
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Locked in the house, Edmund deciphers the ledger page from the coffin: Abigail's own accounting of everyone sworn to silence—including a Wren ancestor who profited most. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the shepherd was always the wolf.

chapters.title: Night of the Descendants
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the founders' annual dinner, Cordelia publicly reads the ledger while Theo streams it live. Silas's allies fracture; one produces proof of the 1987 murder. Emotional beat: the town's gilded unity shattering in real time.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Orchard
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Silas flees to burn the last evidence at the orchard where Abigail's escape began; Edmund pursues him through frost-killed rows, recording everything. Emotional beat: adrenaline and grief colliding as past and present overlap.

chapters.title: The Confession Episode
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Cornered, Silas confesses on tape—not just to recent murders but to the machinery of a century of silencing. Deputies arrive; Cordelia's testimony seals it. Emotional beat: grim triumph that costs Edmund her naivety forever.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. The town holds a funeral for the real Abigail, honoring the woman rather than the legend. Edmund publishes the full series, refusing to soften it. Emotional beat: mourning and release; truth offered as the only honest monument.

chapters.title: The Witness Stays
chapters.summary: Edmund, POV. Offered a national platform, Edmund instead stays in Marlowe's Crossing, opening a community media workshop with Theo and Cordelia. The final scene: a new anonymous letter arrives—another town, another empty coffin. Emotional beat: belonging earned, curiosity rekindled.
